description: Canonical structural reference for the unified MusashiMap data model. This is not a JSON Schema validator.

global_section_contract.section_identity: Global number plus stable bNcN chapter_id
global_section_contract.staging_rule: A chapter may be registered with a local source above maximum_section without becoming reader-visible. Runtime data must remain gated by reader progress.
global_section_contract.source_title_rule: chapters.title is the first non-empty header of chapters.source_file

characters.name: string
characters.first_section: number|null; global first safe physical introduction

locations.name: string
locations.geographic_confidence: string; evidence-qualified confidence or unresolved reason

novel_trigger.spoiler_safe_until: number; global section at which this context is safe

character_wiki_entries.display_name_by_section: object keyed by global reveal section; optional progressive reader-facing name
character_wiki_entries.current_by_section: object keyed by global section; cumulative narrative context

relationships.first_section: number; global first safe reveal threshold

reader_progress.maximum_section: number; authoritative last published global section

integrity_rules: Every cross-book chapter reference uses bNcN; legacy numeric fields may exist only during migration.
Global section numbers are contiguous from 1 through 112 and chapter IDs are unique across all seven books.
Every registered chapter resolves to exactly one local source_file and its title matches that file's first non-empty header exactly.
Registration beyond reader-progress.maximum_section is staging metadata, not publication or permission to expose dependent data.
Micro-wiki and relationship first_section fields are global reveal thresholds and must not exceed the authoritative reader maximum when rendered.
Character-wiki display names and summaries are progressive data and must be filtered at the same publication boundary as events and states.
characters lists physical participants in an event; referenced_characters is used for named people involved only through letters, reports, memories or other non-present references.
Route geometry requires at least one physical event participant; referenced-only reports cannot create cartographic movement lines.
groups lists physically present narrative collectives; referenced_groups is used for collectives mentioned but not present.
character-state location is the physically established cartographic position at the end of the chapter; reported-only positions must use location:null and last_known_location when useful.
location_status values such as reported_position, unknown and departed_* must not be interpreted as physical presence.
character-state destination must not expose a future movement that is first established in a later chapter.
companions represent physical co-presence in the stated narrative state, not people merely mentioned in dialogue or reports.
appearance/presence without an established origin must not be encoded as a confirmed movement edge.
historical context is separate from novel evidence; external sources may explain a named historical entity but must not be used to invent narrative facts.
historical works are first-class contextual entities and are not modeled as characters or factions.
historical_status never implies narrative presence or map presence.
main-cast membership never implies physical presence.
unresolved locations do not receive invented coordinates.
hinagura and hinagura_stockade are distinct identifiers: the former denotes the broader area and the latter the specific fortified site.
locations persist from their first narrative appearance through the end of Book VII unless explicitly retired by future research rules.
